title: Good quality table cloth. Vibrant colors.
text: Good quality table cloth. Vibrant colors.. This is a good quality table cloth.  It lays well on the table and the colors are vibrant.  I'm not giving it 5 stars because $20 is too much money for a tablecloth.  I am looking forward to using it for the 4th of July.  I would value it at about $12 at the most.  Same for the other size I received.

product_metadata.title: DII Patriotic Stripes Tabletop Collection, Stain Resistant & Waterproof, Tablecloth, 60x84, Red, White, & Blue
features: INDOOR & OUTDOOR USE: Enjoy a quality tablecloth that is stain resistant and waterproof measuring 60 x 84-inch, made of 100% polyester with a 1" hem, seats 6-8 people
EASY TO CLEAN: Material can be wiped clean or machine washed on gentle cycle, tumble dry low and Low iron if needed; use again and again
ENJOY WARMER WEATHER: Bring life to your patio or deck with vibrant table top options to host gatherings and share food
ADDS A FINISHING TOUCH: Various designs available to create a look to match your personality, use season after season
GET MORE FROM YOUR TABLE: Protect the surface of your tabletop from scratches, stains, and burns by using runners, placemats, or tablecloths
description: DII outdoor tabletop collections are made of 100% polyester material that is both stain resistant and waterproof. Made to last season after season so you can enjoy for many years to come this collection has quality in every detail. With generously hemmed edges, mitered corners, and color fast ink our product will hold up to continuous use. Material is also machine washable so if you want to simply wipe up a spill or need a more thorough cleaning simply throw in the wash and tumble on low, low iron if needed. Zippered tablecloths and runners are available for use of a patio umbrella. Flap falls over zipper for a seamless look. Colors and patterns are carefully thought out and chosen to be on point and within trend for spring and summer seasons, or use all year round indoor, depending on your need.
